title: SLA Decomposition & GPU Orchestration Decision Guide for Enterprise Dedicated Intakes
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a structured decision guide that decomposes customer SLA requests (p99 latency, tail latency SLOs, throughput guarantees) into determinative inputs for reserved throughput, GPU-class selection, and scaling policy templates. The guide should be usable by Solutions Engineering during intake calls and by PMs when negotiating enterprise contracts. Deliverables: intake questionnaire, scoring rubric, GPU-class mapping, three scaling policy templates (conservative / balanced / aggressive), and examples for burst amortization and fallback orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: Intake questionnaire covers latency distribution, 95/99 percentiles, request size distribution, concurrency profile, peak/steady ratios, and data residency/security constraints
Scoring rubric converts customer signals into a single risk-and-cost score and recommends reserved throughput bands and GPU families
GPU-class mapping includes at least 3 families (high-memory FP16, quantized MT, and inference-optimized / low-latency) with expected token/sec estimates for common model sizes
Scaling policy templates provide autoscale thresholds, burst credit calculation, cooldowns, and graceful fallback order (compatible model variants, region routing, reduced context-length mode)
Guide passes review with Solutions Engineering and Runtime leads and is referenced in at least one intake call within two weeks of publish
proposal_summary: We will formalize how SLA targets translate into reserved throughput commitments and GPU-class decisions. The core idea is SLA decomposition: break high-level SLOs into measurable inputs (avg tokens/sec, tail request concurrency, cold-start risk, acceptable quality degradation). Use a weighted scoring matrix to surface recommended GPU families and reserved throttle bands. Include guardrails for cost-sensitive customers and a decision tree for fallback orchestration when capacity is constrained.
intake_questionnaire: Expected RPS and percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for inference responses
Typical prompt & response token lengths (avg, 95th percentile)
Concurrency expectation: steady vs. burst ratio and burst duration
Tolerance for tail latency: firm SLA (e.g., p99 < 200ms) or soft target
Model family preference or constraints (open models, quantized variants, custom weights)
Availability requirements (monthly uptime SLA) and penalty expectations
Planned rollout pattern (pilot -> ramp -> steady) and expected ramp cadence
scoring_matrix: Weighing: latency sensitivity (35%), throughput scale (30%), cost-sensitivity (15%), availability/region constraints (10%), workload predictability (10%)

Example: Customer A: p99 target 150ms (latency sensitivity = high -> 35 pts), bursty traffic (throughput = high -> 25 pts), cost-sensitive = medium -> 10 pts; aggregated score 70 -> recommend reserved band B (4x baseline) on GPU family G2
Reserved band tiers: Band A = baseline (1x), Band B = moderate (2-4x), Band C = high (5-10x). Map bands to GPU families based on memory and latency characteristics.
recommended_gpu_classes: G-LOWLAT: inference-optimized low-latency (best for strict p99 targets, lower batch throughput) - e.g., 8-bit optimized kernels, ideal for short contexts
G-HIGHTHRU: high-throughput accelerators (best for long context / high tokens/sec; good for batching and quantized models)
G-MEMHEAVY: memory-optimized family (required for very large models or long context lengths where KV cache dominates memory footprint)
Fallback variants: quantized / distilled model variants and multi-GPU sharding patterns
scaling_policy_templates: Conservative: small headroom (1.2x baseline), slow autoscale (5 minute cooldown), prefer warm pool reservations, conservative burst credit (short bursts only), immediate fallback to lower-latency model variant on sustained overload

Balanced: moderate headroom (2-4x baseline), 2-minute cooldown, mixed warm + reactive scaling, burst credit supports multi-minute spikes, fallback order: regional reroute -> compatible quantized model -> throttling with graceful degrade

Aggressive: large headroom (5-10x), rapid autoscale (30s cooldown), optimistic burst amortization, supports preemptible capacity for transient spikes, fallback order: model variants only for quality-preserving swaps
rollback_and_fallback: Define graceful degradation steps: lower sampling temperature / truncated context -> swap to quantized model -> route to lower-tier region -> shed non-critical requests
Instrument feature flags and canary percentages to steer traffic away from overloaded pools
SLA-anchored rollback: if p99 breaches for >5 minutes after autoscale, trigger escalation playbook and offer customer temporary credits or scheduled dedicated ramp
